questionList.title: Time Complexity of QuickSort
questionList.prompt:
What is the average-case time complexity of QuickSort?

```python
def quicksort(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1: return arr
    pivot = arr[len(arr)//2]
    left = [x for x in arr if x < pivot]
    middle = [x for x in arr if x == pivot]
    right = [x for x in arr if x > pivot]
    return quicksort(left) + middle + quicksort(right)
```
options: O(n log n) — divide-and-conquer with balanced partitions
O(n²) — always quadratic regardless of pivot choice
O(n) — linear scan through the array once
O(log n) — only the recursive depth matters
questionList.answer: O(n log n) — divide-and-conquer with balanced partitions

questionList.title: Merge Sort Space Complexity
questionList.prompt:
What is the space complexity of Merge Sort?

```python
def merge_sort(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1: return arr
    mid = len(arr) // 2
    left = merge_sort(arr[:mid])
    right = merge_sort(arr[mid:])
    return merge(left, right)
```
options: O(n) — requires additional arrays for merging at each level
O(1) — merges in place without extra memory
O(log n) — only the recursion stack matters
O(n²) — each merge creates n² temporary arrays
questionList.answer: O(n) — requires additional arrays for merging at each level

questionList.title: Design a Scalable Notification System
questionList.prompt:
## System Design: Notification System

Design a notification system that can send push notifications, emails, and SMS to millions of users.

**Describe your approach covering:**

1. Overall architecture — what components are needed?
2. How do you handle different notification channels (push, email, SMS)?
3. How do you ensure delivery reliability and handle failures?
4. How do you prevent overwhelming users with too many notifications?
5. How would you scale this to handle 1M notifications per minute?

Provide concrete design decisions with reasoning.
questionList.answer:
1. Event-driven architecture: Kafka for ingestion, worker pools per channel, template engine, user preference service. API gateway for admin/internal calls.

2. Strategy pattern: each channel (APNs/FCM for push, SES/SendGrid for email, Twilio for SMS) as a separate service. Message queue per channel for isolation.

3. Retry with exponential backoff, dead letter queue for permanent failures, idempotency keys to prevent duplicates, delivery status tracking.

4. User preference service (opt-in/out per channel), rate limiting per user, priority tiers (transactional > marketing), quiet hours support.

5. Kafka partitions scale with users, auto-scaling workers based on queue depth, database sharding by user_id for preferences, CDN for push certificate management, Redis for rate limit counters.
